summary: Michaux State Forest lookout built 1930, toppled by vandals in 1973, and rebuilt as an 80-ft Aermotor in 1975; gated, with access by permission.

facts.design: 80-ft Aermotor LS-40K with a catwalk on one side (1975 replacement); the 1930 original was toppled in 1973

access.note: Register visit report (2018): tower is gated; permission needed to access; security system in place. A hiking guide notes part of the fence has been pulled up, which is not permission.

visit.trail_note: Gated; visitors must get permission (register visit report, 2018)

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

events.note: Original tower built with a road to the summit and a stone house for the towerman; register says 80-ft Aermotor, the hiking guide says a 90-ft iron tower
Two women manned the tower in May 1943 during a wartime manpower shortage, the first time women staffed it
Lookout reported a 20-acre fire; 30 firefighters and 20 Quincy High School students put it out that day
Vandals cut the legs of the 90-ft tower with hacksaws and felled it. Register dates the attack to October 29, 1973; the newspaper report refers to a Sunday night
New 80-ft Aermotor tower erected on the site; register gives the cost as $45,800; hiking guide names Forest Builders as the construction contractor
Vandals smashed the windows in the tower
Register visit July 12, 2018: good condition, staffed sometimes, gated with permission required

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field gives 1975 for the current tower. The original tower dates to 1930 in the register description and in the Appalachian Trail history. Both dates describe different structures on the same site.

Sources give 80 ft (register, 1930 tower), 90 ft (Appalachian Trail history for the 1930 and 1973 towers and the 1973 newspaper), about 100 ft (1942 survey), and 75 ft (1943 newspaper). The record's 24.4 m matches only the current 1975 tower.
The register dates the felling to October 29, 1973. The newspaper report on the arrests, dated November 3, 1973 on the Forest Lookouts page, refers to a Sunday night attack.
The register names the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. The Forest Lookouts page heading names the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry. The register is used here.
A 2017 state blog post says the tower is not currently manned. The July 2018 register visit says staffed sometimes. These are different dates.
The register says gated and permission needed. The hiking guide says the fence has been pulled up in part. Treated as not open to public climbing.

notes_for_editor: Heights and the 1973 date conflict between sources, and the story says so. The 1930 build comes from the register description and the Appalachian Trail history; the register's Built field says 1975. The 2017 PA blog closely follows the register text, so it is not independent for the 1975 cost or dates. The hiking guide's access note conflicts with the register's gated status; it is noted, not used as permission. Current staffing and access are as of 2018 and need a fresh check. The lookout's Storymap entry was not read.
